front.title: The Latch Protocol for Remote Door Locks

abstract.t: This document specifies Latch, a line-based protocol between a controller and the door locks it manages. It defines the states of a lock, the messages that change them, and the lockout that protects a lock against guessed codes.

section.name: Introduction
section.t: A building has many doors, and each door has a lock. A controller sends Latch messages to the locks over a local network and receives their status.

section.name: Terminology
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 when, and only when, they appear in all capitals, as shown here.

dl.dd: A device that holds a door closed and answers Latch messages.
The system that sends Latch messages to locks.
A string of four to eight digits that a person presents to unlock a door.
A state in which a lock refuses every code for a time.

section.name: Lock States
section.t: A lock MUST be in exactly one of the states "locked", "unlocked" and "lockout".
A lock MUST start in the state "locked" when it is powered on.
An unlocked lock SHOULD return to the state "locked" after ten seconds without a message.

section.name: Messages
section.t: Each message is one line of ASCII text. The syntax uses ABNF .
section.sourcecode: message = unlock-request / lock-request / status-request unlock-request = "UNLOCK" SP door-id SP code CRLF lock-request = "LOCK" SP door-id CRLF status-request = "STATUS" SP door-id CRLF door-id = 1*16(ALPHA / DIGIT / "-") code = 4*8DIGIT

section.name: Unlock
section.t: A lock MUST compare the code of an unlock request with its stored codes in time that does not depend on the code.
A lock MUST NOT unlock while it is in lockout ().

section.name: Status
section.t: A lock MUST answer a status request with its state and the number of failed attempts since it last unlocked.

section.name: Lockout
section.t: After five rejected codes in a row, a lock MUST enter lockout.
A lockout SHOULD last one minute. Should the controller be able to change the duration?

section.name: Security Considerations
section.t: A code travels in clear text on the local network. Deployments SHOULD carry Latch over an encrypted link. This needs a requirement anchor of its own.

section.name: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document has no IANA actions.
